narrative.overview:
The deck is an arrivals board: matte black, edge to edge, behind a hairline steel rule. Not a slide that resembles one — the actual object, with rows that report status in the board's own language and figures set in fixed columns that compare cleanly down a page.

The fiction was chosen because its native context *is* the room the deck is shown in: a departure board is the one object designed to be read simultaneously by a hall full of people standing at different distances. Legible from the back, high contrast under bad light, figures in fixed cells — constraints the board solved decades ago in hardware.

It also settles the status palette without argument. Amber means attention, red means this one costs you, green means nominal, white means unremarkable. And because the board is matte and painted, the surface cannot drift into the glowing dark-keynote look every AI-generated dark deck lands on. There is no glow in this world.

An earlier revision built the fiction out literally — split-flap cells with hinge lines, a brushed steel housing with bolt heads, and a flip cascade on every slide change. That was too much theatre for a ten-minute cost talk; the mechanism started reading as the subject. It was cut deliberately. What survives is the part doing the work: the matte ground, the status palette, the row grammar, and fixed columns.

rules.name: The Still Board Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a slide animates. Slides replace each other; their contents are simply there. The split-flap cascade was cut on purpose — do not reintroduce it, and do not add a replacement. No fades, no counting-up figures, no reveals. The only motion in this deck is the person talking.

rules.name: The Status-Only Rule
rules.body: Amber, red, and green mean state. A figure is amber because the room should look at it, never because amber looks good.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow spread as light, no neon, no blur halo, no gradient text. Depth comes from hairline rules and one-step surface changes.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere, at all. Zero occurrences is the invariant.

rules.name: The Rows-Not-Cards Rule
rules.body: If content is a comparison, it is a table of rows with shared columns and a status chip. Cards are for worlds that need containers; this one has a board.

rules.name: The Caps Rule
rules.body: Display and headline type is uppercase, tracked wide, set plainly on the board ground. Caps are what make a headline legible from the back.

rules.name: The Container-Query Rule
rules.body: Type scales in cqw against the board's own inline size, never vw. The projector's aspect ratio is unknown.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Comparable figures are mono with tabular-nums. On a board, a column that does not line up is a broken board.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears on the brandmark, the live rail segment, and focus rings. Three places. Never a status, never a fill.

antiPatterns: Glow, neon, gradient text, or blur — the object is matte
Body text in a bordered box (that is a card)
A fourth status colour, or a status colour used decoratively
Any animation whatsoever — see The Still Board Rule
The retired −11° skew from the previous world
Signal Blue outside the brandmark, live rail, and focus ring
